column2: In the thunderbolt circle, above and below, from the first seed — then the cow-formed lunar form, raining a stream of nectar,
entering through the Brahma-aperture: the practitioner should contemplate. At head, mouth, throat, heart, navel, private part, thighs, knees and feet
the mantra-master should place the first seed, with the forefinger and the rest again and again. Moon above, lotus below — the body is the seed-form;
one who knows this has no death, no diseases or fevers. One should worship and recite her, having placed, meditating on the goddess a hundred and eight times.
I shall tell the mudras: the Pranita and others, the Pranita is remembered as fivefold. Having made the hands interlocked, one should drop the thumbs in the middle;
the forefinger touching the head, one should place it above the head; this is called Pranita; one should bring it to the heart region;
upward in the middle of the little fingers with the seed end, twice-born know; having applied the forefingers in the middle, many joined one another,
one should insert the tip of the elder one in the middle — this is called Bhedani. Having bound it at the navel region one should then raise the thumbs;
the Karali is the great mudra to be applied by the mantra-master at the heart. Again as before, the elder finger bound and touching, one should raise;
it is called Vajratunda; one should bind at the vajra region; with both hands one should bind at the wrist;
having spread three and three, it is called the Vajra mudra. Staff, sword, discus and mace mudras are remembered by form;
with the thumb one should press three; the trident is upward; one with the middle finger up is declared Shakti;
arrow, boon, bow, noose, burden, bell, conch, goad, fearlessness, lotus — twenty-eight in all;
Mohani, Mokshani, Jvalini, Amritabhaya — the five mudras declared; one should apply them in worship and oblation.
Having uttered the root knowledge going through wind and sky, twice-born, one should worship again with the first on the pericarp.
Five and five should be worshipped each with their own mantras; one should place the eight world-guardians outside, in the womb-mandala.
Ending with a letter, mounted on fire, divided by the sixth vowel, covered with the fifteenth, one should join with their own names;
quickly one should worship Simha on the pericarp with scents and the rest for prosperity; one should surround with eight pots consecrated by the eight-hundred-fold mantra;
having recited the mantra eight thousand times and a tenth for the limbs, one should make the oblation in the fire-pit and move it with the fire mantra;
one should cast the fire with the heart-mantra; one should remember the power in the middle going into the fire. One should offer the conception, male-begetting and birth rites;
with the heart, a hundred; one in the secret; one should produce the flame in the secret limb. By the full oblation of the knowledge the Shiva-fire becomes blazing.
One should offer with the root mantra, and a hundred for limbs by a tenth; then one should offer to the Goddess; then one should have the disciple enter;
having struck with the weapon one should then place the secret limbs; one equipped with knowledge-limbs should be engaged in the knowledge-limbs;
one should have the disciple throw a flower and bring him to the fire-pit; with barley, grains, sesame and ghee one should offer the root knowledge a hundred times.
First the oblation of stationary state, then reptile; birds, beasts, animals; human and Brahma state;
Vishnu-state and Rudra-state — at the end there is a full oblation. With a single oblation the disciple becomes initiated;
authority arises thus; hear now liberation. When the mantra-master, standing on Sumeru, stands in the Sadashiva station,
he should offer in the supreme, self-established, ten hundred acts and non-acts; by the full oblation that yogi is not tainted by dharma and adharma,
and goes to liberation, the supreme state from which one does not return. As water cast in water, so the embodied one's head;
one should make the consecration with pots; he shares victory, kingdom and all. A maiden and a Brahmin woman are to be honored; one should give a fee to the teacher and the rest.
One should worship a thousand; having done worship day by day, with sesame, ghee and city oblation, the goddess Shri becomes the granter of desires;
she gives abundant enjoyments and whatever else is desired. Having recited a lakh of syllables one becomes lord of treasures;
with double, kingdom; with triple, a Yakshini; with fourfold, Brahma-state, then Vishnu's station;
with sixfold, great success; with a single lakh, destroyer of sin; having recited ten for body-purity, from a hundred the fruit of bathing in holy places.
On cloth or on an image, or on a platform one should quickly worship her. A hundred, a thousand, ten thousand are declared in recitation and oblation.
Having recited thus by rule, one should offer a lakh with buffalo, goat or ram meat, or with human-born (offering) or city;
with sesame, barley, parched rice, rice, wheat, and mango, with Shri-fruit joined with ghee, having offered, one should practice the vow.
At midnight, girded, with sword, bow, arrows and the like, in a single garment, in a varied one, or red, yellow or black,
or blue cloth — with those very one should worship the Goddess. One should go to the south; at the door the wise one should give the offering;
with the messenger mantra at the door and the rest, at a lone tree, in a cremation ground. So all desires are obtained; the king enjoys the whole earth.
With the threefold yoga, the body equipped by the Goddess, one knows the success-giving mantras and the many that have come from the prelude.
Mantras are remembered in each scripture; their applications there are rare. The first letter is the teacher's; it is not described earlier.
In the prelude one-letter, two-letter, three-letter and so on arose; lines crossing and upward should divide into four and four;
nine compartments arise thus, in the middle region these; having placed clockwise, one should then break the prelude.
By the order of the prelude, whoever obtains the prelude — the successes of that practitioner are held in his fist;
the three worlds are at the foot of his feet; he gains the nine-continent earth. Having written on a skull the Shiva-principle all around,
or on a cremation-ground rag, the mantra-knower having gone outside, should write the name in the middle standing on the pericarp;
one should heat with khadira embers, standing on birch bark with the feet; in seven days one would bring all the three worlds with moving and unmoving.
In the womb of the thunderbolt-casket, in the twelve-spoked, one should write: in the middle the name inside, enclosed by Sadashiva;
on a wall, board or stone slab with turmeric — stopping of speech, stopping of movement, and stopping of armies result.
Having written with poison-blood on a cremation-ground potsherd, the wise one: a six-cornered diagram pressed by a staff, joined all around with power;
this would soon kill the enemy struck in the cremation ground. He makes a cut of the nation; one should place the enemy in the middle of the wheel.
The power in the wheel-edge limbs removes the enemy by the enemy's name; with the Tarkshya seed alone one should write in the middle of a sword
the Vidarbha enemy's name written with cremation-ground charcoal; in seven days one should subdue the country, strike with corpse-ash.
In breaking, cutting and killing he would be Shiva. The Taraka is declared the eye; one should employ it in peace and nourishment.
This is an application of burning and the like; one should also draw a Shakini. From the middle to the west, joined with the crooked-beaked,
diseases like leprosy and the rest it destroys, no doubt. From the middle to the north one should recite by the Karali binding;
one should protect one's knowledge when the opponent is Shiva. Then having placed from the west and the rest, it destroys fever and cough;
from the north to the middle heaviness arises in the banyan; from the east to the middle it makes lightness in a moment.
Written on birch bark with gorochana, this city is thunderbolt-filled; with the mantra seeds in order one should make protection on the bodies.
Wrapped with gold of feeling, this protection destroys death; worn, it subdues obstacles, sins and enemies and gives good fortune and life;
it gives victory in gambling and battle, in Indra's army, no doubt. It gives sons to barren women, like another wish-jewel.
One should subdue other countries and conquer the earth, the kingdom. "Phat strim kshem hum" — by a lakh recitation yakshas and the rest become subject.
Vakra, Vikatanana, then "hum" the first, destroyer of obstacles; smoky-colored, Mahendra and the rest; outside, worship of the Lord of obstacles.
I shall tell the worship of Tripura: Asitanga, Ruru, Chanda, Krodha, Unmatta, Kapali, Bhishana in order,
Samhara, Bhairava — the chief Brahmis; the short ones are Bhairavas; Brahmani and Shanmukha long ones; in the southeast and the rest the Vatukas in order:
Samayaputra Vatuka, Yoginiputraka likewise, Siddhaputra Vatuka, and the fourth Kulaputra;
Hetuka and Kshetrapala, Tripurantaka second; Agnivetala, Agnijihva, Karali, Kalalochana,
Ekapada, Bhimaksha; "aim kshem," the Preta, her seat; "aim hrim" two — Tripura seated in a lotus posture,
holding fearlessness and a book, on the left a boon and a rosary. With the root mantra the heart and the rest; the net-filled one, fulfiller of desire.
Having written the name in the middle of a cow and in the middle of an eight-petalled lotus, one should write with cremation-ground charcoal on a cremation-ground cloth,
having meditated on his image made of pyre-charcoal paste, placing it in the belly and wrapping with blue threads, the banishing would result.

Om homage to the Lady Jvalamalini, surrounded by hosts of vultures, svaha — a man who goes to battle reciting this mantra is visibly victorious. "Om shrim hrim klim, homage to Shri" — in the north and so on, Ghrini and Surya are to be worshipped in a four-petalled lotus,
Aditya and Prabhavati, refuge of the golden mountain and sweetness. "Om hrim, homage to Gauri" — the Gauri mantra does all, by oblation, meditation, recitation and worship.
Red, four-armed, with noose and boon in the right hand, joined with goad and fearlessness — a man, having prayed to her with a perfected self, ...
